physical_mismatches.reason: 3D integration with Memory-on-Logic (MOL) configuration introduces vertical stacking that multiplies power density by die count (2 dies), reducing die footprint by 0.665× but increasing power density by 1.37×, changing thermal resistance profile compared to 2D baseline

Silicon logic layer thinning from 100 µm to 5 µm to enable nTSV interconnects degrades lateral heat spreading; thermal conductivity of thinned logic die drops from 140 W/m·K to 100 W/m·K and exhibits ballistic/quasiballistic phonon scattering effects below 100 µm, causing 6.7% temperature rise in logic die and 3.1% in memory die

Addition of low thermal conductivity BEOL stack layer (1.2 W/m·K, 2.85 µm thickness) between dies increases thermal resistance path from logic layer to heatsink, raising logic die temperature 3°C higher than memory die despite identical power per unit area

Paper uses lumped thermal RC network model in HotSpot v7.0 which assumes uniform power density within functional blocks; does not resolve sub-block spatial heterogeneity or account for detailed 3D heat flow coupling across nTSV interfaces and F2F bonding uniformity

Steady-state thermal analysis only; no transient thermal coupling effects, thermal cycling fatigue, or dynamic workload variations modeled despite multi-core activity pattern sensitivity demonstrated in Section III.C

studio_assumptions: Ambient temperature fixed at 27°C (representative value for domain)

Thermal design power (TDP) baseline of 40 W for 2D-SOC applies directly to 3D-SOC power scaling analysis; 3D power consumption reduced by 0.913× due to shorter interconnects but power density increased by 1.37× due to footprint reduction by 0.665×
C4 micro-bumps and solder balls replaced with single equivalent thermal conductivity stack (1.25 and 16.67 W/m·K effective)
Face-to-face (F2F) wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding pitch maintained at full 6-metal-layer stack (M6M6, 12 layers) with effective thermal conductivity of F2F via layer
Polymer thermal interface material (PTIM) properties: 100 µm thickness, 7 W/m·K constant thermal conductivity independent of thickness or pressure
Heat spreader and heatsink convective resistance values: 0.17 K/W (heatsink to ambient), 50 K/W (PCB to ambient) remain constant across 2D and 3D configurations
Silicon thermal conductivity values: memory die 140 W/m·K (100 µm), logic die 100 W/m·K (5 µm) assumed isotropic and thickness-dependent per Figure 5(b) ballistic scattering model
Tile-level power breakdown (Figure 3: cores 39%, interconnects 27%, I$ 13%, SPM 11%, others 10%) representative of full 256-core, 64-tile MemPool architecture under full workload
All thermal coupling between logic and memory dies in 3D stacking treated as one-dimensional resistance path through BEOL stack; no lateral heat spreading between dies modeled
